You can absolutely tell an agent to fix an issue, and it will fix that issue, but the vast majority of the time that solution will be by adding code to cover the specific symptom in the bug report. It rarely considers or recommends solutions that have tradeoffs that may change behavior but will eliminate an entire class of similar bugs. This is mostly a problem of agents not having the autonomy of managing an entire project and having the ability to make tradeoffs to increase simplicity or maintainability, but when given that autonomy no AI model I've used uses that privilege to write simpler, more maintainable code. reply davnicwil 15 hours ago | parent | next [–] I think this gets to something quite fundamental which is in the information loss when delegating a task in plain English. It takes a lot of skill on both sides to negotiate this even in an ongoing conversational loop. There comes a point of course where essentially doing this communication and negotiation is equivalent to the work. Fixing the root cause and doing so with the least amount of code often is contradictory. Including instructions to make suggestions to improve code maintainability will cause the AI to do it every single time it makes a change, even if it's completely unnecessary, drowning out useful suggestions in noise. When a bug is caused by a requirement elsewhere in the application, current models are more likely to break that functionality and implement a fix anyway rather than pause and get confirmation on the requirement. They may leave a note about the broken functionality at the end, but by that point the AI has already been iterating with an incorrect assumption. Any code the agent wrote in the same turn is going to be tainted by that assumption and it often does not remove or rewrite that code when given clarified requirements. It's tempting to blame all AI issues on prompting because it's the only thing that we're able to control, but if a task falls into the long tail of work unable to be satisfactorily completed with AI, there's no prompt that will work. When there's always the alternative of doing the work yourself, it's not worthwhile to spend the tokens or time to get an AI model to do something after the first two or three prompts. reply td521534f12 15 hours ago | prev | next [–] All my solo project backlogs _are_ empty.
